items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: like Ken Burns’ jazz documentary, it stops at 1955 or wherever.

ctx.x: Okay. Do you have a feeling about jazz education these days?

Well having taught in the schools, some schools in the U.S., and I taught for a semester as a guest professor in Graz, Austria, at KUG there, which, it’s a very prestigious, one of the only jazz schools, maybe the only one in Austria. And I prefer the European. Because it seems to me that the educational system in the U.S. stops at — like Ken Burns’ jazz documentary, it stops at 1955 or wherever. They don’t even go into the sixties and beyond. So maybe that’s changed now or it maybe in other programs, but the…
Are you talking about like jazz schools?
